prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: the first viewport of a page plus the beginning of the next section. A real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The attached reference images are screenshots of the SAME website's already-built homepage. Carry over exactly: the header (the script wordmark "Birdcar" at left in a forward-leaning connected brush script; at right the nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a compact canary-yellow pill button "Book a free Walkthrough →" with ink text), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy, tight, confident grotesk (Mona Sans) for every heading and body line, white pill tags with soft shadows, canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and things in motion, teal #5fb8bf only for a resolved state, and the premium matte isometric miniature render style (soft studio daylight, fine architectural-model detail, pale wood, matte stone, teal-cyan floor tiles, a small canary). Do NOT copy the reference's content: no homepage headline, no full office diorama, no logo strip, no model shelf.

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days of the conversation the visitor receives a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. The visitor's job on this page: understand the offer and book a time.

STRUCTURE, in reading order (a booking-desk layout: the calendar is in the first viewport):
1. Header, about 80px, exactly as the reference.
2. First viewport, two columns.
LEFT column (x 80 to 690): headline about 64px, ink, two lines: "An hour on the work. A report you can use." Below, a paragraph at about 19px, ink-soft: "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble. Within three business days you get my recommendations in writing." Then one short line at about 19px, medium weight: "The hour is about your work. If you want to talk about hiring me, you'll bring it up, not me." Below that a compact white card (10px radius, soft shadow) titled "Your Walkthrough report" listing three rows separated by hairlines: "What's happening", "What I recommend", and "Where I'd start" (this third row sits on a canary-yellow highlight). A small muted line under it: "In writing within three business days. Yours to keep."
RIGHT column (x 760 to 1460, y 110 to 900): the dominant object: a large white booking calendar card, 14px radius, soft ambient shadow, showing the heading "The Walkthrough", a line "About 60 minutes · Video call or in person", a month grid "October 2026" with a handful of available dates marked by thin ink rings, and a column of time slots. The card rests on a small premium matte isometric miniature: a corner of the owner's desk in pale wood with an open brass birdcage, and a small canary perched on the calendar card's top-left corner. One contact shadow grounds it.
3. Bottom band (y 900 to 1024) on white: the start of the next section, three numbered steps in a row: "1 Choose a time." "2 Walk me through it." "3 Keep the report." each with one short line of muted body text.

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the calendar on the miniature desk; everything else holds still in the site's grammar. Premium, adult, precise. Not cute, no toy proportions. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
